page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head centred at the top. Signature at bottom left and catchword at bottom right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: tator,non plagiarius collector censeatur: sic si[?] aeterum[?] locupletissimorum thesauris, vel pretiosissima quaeque accipiat, ut ea si non angustiore, nova tamen forma tum immutata propria faciat. Et quemadmodum ex Herculis pascuis in speluncam Gerionis boues auersis vestigiis ne fortum[?] proderetur Cacus, olim deduxisse fertur, sic ex doctissimorum hominum scriptis in nostras commentationes ea transferre licebit: quae si alio no mero, alia methodo exponantur, non est vereundum ne nocis alicuius indicio, unde sint depromptae significetur. Ea enim est hominum ingeniosorum, & prope diuinorum solers & prudes[?] industria non vulgarium scriptorum laboriosa quidem, sed fastidiosa diligentia. Ea fuit ante aliquot annos Ioannis Fernelij in constituenda arte medica & explicandis (si fieri possit) Abditis rerum causis dexteritas, ut vel in conferendis ceteris opinionibus, ceteres Fernelij ore loqui videantur, vel in suis afferendis Fernelius index aequissimus novam sententiam ferat, determinationemq; constituat. Denique nihil sit in huius scriptis, quod vere Fernelianum non sit: sive enim dicendi species genus, ingenij flumen, summam vim dicendi atque copiam, nullius propriam praeterea in Fernelio agnoscas: sive rationem docendi & vi-am, quam infequitur, infpicias, ars pulcherrima, quae hactenus partibus suis diuulsa proponebatur, conuenienti & apta earundem connexione, integra & longe uenustior exhibetur: sive etiam sententiarum axiomata & ef-fata pendas, pleraque omnia nova & inaudita, ac mere Fernelianaiudicabis. page.notes: Uncertain readings: "sic si aeterum" (the word after "si" is faint; "1" may be a ligature), "fortum" (could be read differently), "prudes" (a mark may be a contraction), and the catchword "ioꝛ&". "Fernelianaiudicabis" appears to lack a space between "Ferneliana" and "iudicabis" in the print. "ceteres" is printed "aeteres" and "ceteri" is printed with a slightly blurred letter; both are transcribed with the likely reading. The hyphen after "ha" and "ef" is taken from the line ends. Printed "viam" is split as "vi-am" across lines.
